282033.name: Chabad Jewish Community Center of Riverside
282033.note: Lubavitch.com, 19 May 2005 ('New Chabad Representatives to Riverside, California'): 'Rabbi and Mrs. Shmuel Fuss of Brooklyn, New York, were appointed Chabad representatives to Riverside, California. The couple will establish a Chabad House to serve the local community, and the Jewish student body at Riverside University.' Its chabad.org listing went up May 23 2005, and Lubavitch News Service (2 Dec 2005) counts the University of California, Riverside among the campuses that got Chabad teams that year. The center's LinkedIn page: 'Founded: 2005' (Rabbi Shmuel and Tzippy Fuss; therebbesimpact.com: 2004 for them, 2005 for the center).

169299.name: Chabad of Chesterfield
169299.note: Lubavitch.com, 25 Aug 2004 ('New Appointments'): 'Lubavitch World Headquarters announces the following new appointments of Chabad-Lubavitch Shluchim: ... Chesterfield, Missouri: Rabbi and Mrs. Avi and Chana Rubenfeld.' St. Louis Jewish Light (2021): serving Chesterfield, Ballwin and Wildwood 'for the past 17 years' (so 2004); again (2 Sept 2022): 'for over 17 years'. Its chabad.org listing went up Sept 1 2004, so it existed by then. Rabbi Avi and Chana'la Rubenfeld. Its own building at 15310 Conway Road (groundbreaking Sept 14 2022, to open summer 2023); before that leased space (not dated here).

349940.name: Chabad @ CSUN
349940.note: Lubavitch News Service, 2 Dec 2005 ('New Chabad Centers Open at University of Kansas and Cal State Northridge', lubavitch.com; CrownHeights.info ran it the next day): 'Rabbi Chaim and Raizel Brook, who are on their way to Northridge, CA, are boxing up the contents of their Brooklyn apartment and brainstorming content for their first Torah classes'; students returning 'from holiday break' would meet them. So they came at the end of 2005 (perhaps the first days of 2006); its chabad.org listing went up Jan 17 2006. Jewish Journal, May 22 2025 ('Rabbis of LA'): Rabbi Chaim Brook is 'now in his 20th year at CSUN', and he and Raizel 'were married in 2004, about a year before they arrived in Northridge', so 2005; therebbesimpact.com agrees.

406831.name: Chabad of West Hills
406831.note: The LA Daily News (on CrownHeights.info, 10 June 2006, 'A new Chabad House, as always, with an open door'): 'The welcome mat will be out Sunday for the grand opening of the Chabad of West Hills, the 19th Chabad center in the San Fernando Valley. The synagogue actually held its first service at sundown June 1 for the Jewish festival of Shavuot'; Rabbi Avi Rabin 'will lead the new Orthodox Jewish congregation'. Its chabad.org listing went up July 24 2006. COLlive, June 6 2013: the gala 'celebrated 7 years since the opening of Chabad of West Hills' (Rabbi Avi and Dena Rabin); the listing number (406831) is from about 2006.

earlier.where: 23747 Roscoe Blvd, West Hills (Chabad of the Valley's directory page; now 6820 Valley Circle Blvd)

476686.name: Chabad Center for Jewish Life
476686.note: Shmais (on CrownHeights.info, 7 Nov 2006, 'New Shluchim To Oregon!'): 'Rabbi & Mrs. Avrohom Yitzchok (A.Y.) Perlstein will IY"H be moving on Shlichus to Salem, Oregon where they will establish a new Chabad House serving the members of the Jewish community of the greater Salem/Keiser area', appointed by the head shliach, Rabbi Moshe Wilhelm. A month later their corporation was registered in Oregon at the Salem address (below). Its chabad.org listing went up 2007-02-13, so it existed by then. Director: Avrohom Yitzchok Perlstein. Oregon Secretary of State record (data.oregon.gov, 'Active Businesses - ALL'): 'CHABAD JEWISH CENTER OF SALEM, INC.' (registry number 39974498), domestic nonprofit corporation, registered Dec 11 2006 at 1370 Crowley Ave SE, Salem (the listing's address); registered agent Avrohom Perlstein (the listing's director).

527027.name: Kennesaw Chabad Jewish Center
527027.note: The Marietta Daily Journal (on CrownHeights.info, 12 Feb 2008, 'Chabad is Opening New Doors'): 'That all changed seven weeks ago, when Rabbi Zalman Charytan, his wife Nechami and their 2-year-old and five-month-old children moved to Acworth from New York. The couple's mission: To establish the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth', so they moved about late December 2007, as the Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007) had planned ('in November'); its chabad.org listing went up Dec 5 2007. Began as the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth. CrownHeights.info, 4 Feb 2008: Rabbi Zalman and Nechami Charytan 'have recently moved on Shlichus to Acworth, GA where they have established the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth serving the Jewish residents of North West Cobb County'; Chabad.org, 23 Nov 2008: the Charytans 'established the Chabad-Lubavitch Jewish Center of Acworth, Ga., this year'. Chabad.org's 'this year' (2008) is taken as the center's first full year; they arrived in December 2007. Today at 3590 Frey Lake Road NW, Kennesaw (when it moved is not stated).

earlier.where: Acworth (the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth)

541856.name: Rohr Chabad Jewish Center
541856.note: Chabad.edu (on CrownHeights.info, 19 Sept 2007, 'New Arrivals Working to Strengthen Jewish Life in West Virginia'): 'Open earlier this year under the direction of Rabbi Zalman and Hinda Gurevitz, the Chabad Jewish Center of Morgantown, W.Va., caters to the university's Jewish students as well as to the city's diverse population'. The Pittsburgh Jewish Chronicle (on CrownHeights.info, 11 Dec 2013): 'For the last six years, the living room in the small, Morgantown, W.Va.' home of the Gurevitzes served as the Chabad House; 'It was Rosenfeld who assigned the Gurevitzes to Morgantown six years ago' (so 2007). Its listing went up Aug 6 2007, which agrees.

1279033.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Goodyear
1279033.note: CrownHeights.info, 6 Sept 2010 ('Announcing New Shluchim to Arizona'): 'Rabbi Berel Zaklikofsky and and wife Chana Rivka of Crown Heights will be moving on Shlichus to Goodyear, AZ', appointed by Rabbi Zalman and Tzippy Levertov, head shluchim to Arizona. CrownHeights.info (27 April 2021): 'In 2010 Rabbi Berel and Chana Zaklikofsky made a lifetime commitment to the Jewish community of Goodyear, AZ, founding the Chabad Jewish Center.' The Jewish News ('Valley View', 17 June 2011, 'Chabad opens center in Goodyear'): they 'moved to Arizona from Brooklyn, N.Y., last week to start Chabad Jewish Center of Goodyear'; before that he 'visited Arizona last December to host a menorah-lighting celebration at Goodyear Community Park'. Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 19 2010. So the work began in 2010 (the appointment, the listing, the December 2010 lighting); the family moved there in June 2011. Now 14295 W La Reata Avenue.

4961934.name: Chabad Passaic Clifton
4961934.note: CrownHeights.info, 11 July 2007 ('New Shluchim to New Jersey'): 'Rabbi Yitzchak and Mrs. Miriam (nee Eber) Sebbag of Crown Heights have just moved on Shlichus to Passaic, NJ where they will establish a new Chabad House and Chai Tots Preschool for the Jewish residents in Passaic and Clifton, New Jersey', appointed by Rabbi Michel Gurkov of Chabad of Passaic County (whom the listing, made Dec 2020, names). Jewish Link, 16 March 2017: 'On February 26, Chabad of Passaic-Clifton held its annual dinner, celebrating 10 years of making a difference' (Rabbi Yitzchak and Miriam Sebbag), so about 2007. Its corporation Chabad of Passaic Clifton Inc has an IRS ruling of Aug 2010.

5590394.name: Chabad of Downtown - South Scottsdale
5590394.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 16 Nov 2022, 'A New Chabad Every Three Days'): a Simchat Torah party (October 2022) 'was the first large event that new shluchim Rabbi Shmuli and Mushkie Bronstein were arranging, having moved to Scottsdale just weeks prior to found Chabad of Downtown—South Scottsdale, a young professionals community under the umbrella of Chabad of Scottsdale'. The Jewish News (4 March 2025): 'The Bronsteins took the helm of the Chabad Young Professionals of Scottsdale group in 2022', and later 'moved to open Chabad of Old Town-South Scottsdale'. Its chabad.org listing (Rabbi Shmuli and Mushkie Bronstein, young professionals) went up Oct 24 2022.

5587788.name: Chabad of Leander
5587788.note: Its chabad.org listing went up Aug 11 2022, and Merkos's list of 'New Shluchim' grants for the year to Nov 2022 (CrownHeights.info, 19 Nov 2022) names 'Shmuel and Nechama Fradel Levertov, Leander, TX', so the work began by 2022 (first mention, the listing). Lubavitch.com (CrownHeights.info, 23 Dec 2024, 'Chabad Opens in Leander, Texas, Amid Tech-Fueled Boom'): a family that moved to Leander in 2021 heard, 'two years after moving to town', of its first-ever public menorah lighting, 'held by Rabbi Shmuly and Nechomele Levertov, who'd just moved to town to found Chabad of Leander' (counted that way, about 2023, so that lighting may have been Chanukah 2022 or 2023). Medium: no report of the start itself.

5805649.name: Chabad of Hewlett Neck & Old Woodmere
5805649.note: Merkos's mid-year list of new shluchim approved for funding (CrownHeights.info, 2 June 2022, 'New Shluchim and Mikvaos Announced – 150 New Grants Awarded') names 'Mendel Gordon – Woodmere, NY', and the IRS recognized 'Chabad Of Hewlett Neck And Old Woodmere Inc' from Nov 2022, so the work began by 2022 (first mention); its chabad.org listing went up Feb 1 2023. Chabad.org on CrownHeights.info, 21 Sept 2023: Chabad of Sea Cliff and Glen Cove 'is the second Chabad House to open on Long Island this year, joining the Chabad of Hewlett Neck and Old Woodmere, which is run by Rabbi Mendel and Goldie Gordon.' That 2023 opening is taken as its house's; the start is 2022. Medium: no report of the start itself.

4887459.name: Chabad of South Austin
4887459.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 12 Nov 2020, 'Despite Pandemic, More Than 100 New Emissaries Join the Ranks of Chabad'): 'Rabbi Mendy and Rikki Hertz have this in mind as they chart new waters in South Austin, Texas'; the pandemic upended their plans, but 'we have been able to meet new people and actually connect with them in a real way ... it has enabled us to operate despite the challenges.' So they were at work in 2020; its chabad.org listing went up Oct 21 2020. Anash.org, 29 Oct 2020 ('New Shluchim to America's Fastest-Growing City'): 'America's fastest-growing city will soon be getting a new Chabad center with the appointment of Rabbi Mendel and Rikki Hertz as the new shluchim to South Austin, Texas', under Rabbi Yosef Levertov, still raising seed money. Shalom Austin (2024): by 2021 another Chabad was needed south of the river.

164329.name: Chabad of the Central Cascades
164329.note: Lubavitch.com, 25 Aug 2004 ('New Appointments'): 'Lubavitch World Headquarters announces the following new appointments of Chabad-Lubavitch Shluchim: ... Issaquah, Washington: Rabbi Shalom D. and Nechama Farkash'; its chabad.org listing went up the same day. Lubavitch.com, 27 Jan 2005 ('Three new centers in Washington State'): 'Just east of Seattle is Issaquah, King County, the new home of Rabbi Sholom Ber and Nechama Farkash.' Its chabad.org listing went up 25 Aug 2004. Lubavitch.com, 17 Sept 2009, says 'In the summer of 2005, Rabbi Shalom Dovber (Berry) and Nechama Farkash arrived in Central Cascades'; the reports of Aug 2004 and Jan 2005 and the 2004 listing outweigh that later account.
